;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Kurdish–Turkish conflict (2015–present)]]
**The [[Turkish Army]] launches a joint air-land [[Kurdish–Turkish_conflict_(1978–present)#External_operations|external operation]] [[Operations Claw-Eagle and Claw-Tiger|Claw-Eagle and Claw-Tiger]] into [[Northern Iraq]] against [[Kurds in Iraq|Kurdish]] [[insurgent]]s. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jun/17/turkey-launches-major-attack-on-kurdish-militants-in-iraq (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Kashmir conflict]], [[India–Pakistan relations]]
**Four civilians are killed following Indian [[Artillery|bombardment]] of territory in [[Pakistan]]-administered [[Kashmir]], according to Pakistani officials. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/pakistan-civilians-killed-indian-shelling-loc-200618072318096.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Actions against memorials in the United Kingdom during the George Floyd protests]], [[Rhodes Must Fall]]
**The [[Oriel College, Oxford|Oriel College]] governing body votes to remove a 109-year-old statue of [[Cecil Rhodes]] from the college grounds amid [[anti-racism]] protests. Campaigners say the statue is a symbol of [[racism]] and British [[imperialism]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/education-53082545 (BBC News)]

;Business and economy
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kazakhstan]], [[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Kazakhstan]]'s [[sovereign wealth fund]] [[Samruk-Kazyna]] announces that plans to sell [[Share (finance)|shares]] in the [[government of Kazakhstan|state]]-run oil and gas company [[KazMunayGaz]] abroad will be delayed from this year to 2022 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic|pandemic]]. [https://reuters.com/article/kazmunaygaz-ipo/update-1-kazakhstan-plans-kazmunaygaz-ipo-in-2022-idINL8N2DU0IO (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[Johns Hopkins University]] says that the death toll due to the COVID-19 pandemic in the [[United States]] has surpassed the number of American casualties during [[World War I]]. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/coronavirus-leaves-more-americans-dead-than-first-world-war-1.4987531 (CTV News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Honduras]]
***[[President of Honduras|President]] [[Juan Orlando Hernández]] is hospitalized for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] and is being treated for [[pneumonia]]. Although receiving medicine via an [[intravenous drip]], the president is claimed to be generally in good health, according to a spokesman for the Health Ministry. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-honduras-president/honduran-president-hospitalized-for-covid-19-treated-for-pneumonia-idUSKBN23O36I?il=0 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Paulinho Paiakan]], leader of the [[Indigenous peoples in Brazil|indigenous]] [[Kayapo]] tribe, dies after being hospitalized with COVID-19 in [[Redenção, Ceará|Redenção]], [[Brazil]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200617-iconic-amazon-indigenous-chief-paiakan-dies-of-virus (France24)]

;International relations
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**[[North Korea]] rejects [[South Korea]]'s offer to send special [[Envoy (title)#Popular parlance|envoys]] to defuse the current tensions on the [[Korea|peninsula]], after having destroyed the [[Inter-Korean Liaison Office]], and says the [[Korean People's Army]] will re-enter the demilitarized [[Kaesong Industrial Region|Kaesong]] and [[Mount Kumgang]] areas. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20200617000200325 (Yonhap)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-southkorea/north-korea-rejects-souths-offer-of-envoys-vows-to-send-back-troops-to-border-idUSKBN23N3GY (Reuters)]
*[[China–Japan relations]]
**[[Japan]] says it will keep a close watch over the disputed [[Senkaku Islands]] after [[China|Chinese]] ships are seen near the islands for 65 days in a row. Chief Cabinet Secretary [[Yoshihide Suga]] says that Japan has protested to China over the issue and that it would respond "calmly and firmly". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-japan-china-suga/japan-to-keep-close-watch-over-disputed-islands-suga-idUSKBN23O144 (Reuters)]
*[[Syria–United States relations]]
**[[U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] announces "toughest sanctions" on [[Syrian president]] [[Bashar al-Assad]] and his wife [[Asma al-Assad|Asma]] in an effort to end the decade-long [[Syrian Civil War|civil war]] in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-syria-security-usa-sanctions/u-s-hits-syria-with-toughest-sanctions-yet-to-push-assad-to-end-war-idUSKBN23O20P?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 United Nations Security Council election]]
**[[Norway]] and [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] win seats in the [[United Nations Security Council]], joining new members [[India]] and [[Mexico]]. [[Canada]], which was considered a favorite, and had strongly campaigned for a seat for four years on the council, fails to get enough votes. Canadian Foreign Minister [[François-Philippe Champagne]] says he is proud of the campaign but declines to comment on the reasons for their loss. [https://apnews.com/8f759f3892fc835be385b6b60035e829 (AP)]

;Law and crime
*[[Papua conflict]], [[2019 Papua protests]]
**A court in [[Indonesia]] sentences Chairman of the [[National Committee for West Papua]] [[Buchtar Tabuni]] and six others to 11 months in prison for [[treason]]. The seven men were charged after they joined [[anti-racism]] protests that swept across two provinces in [[Western New Guinea]] last August. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/indonesian-court-announce-verdict-west-papua-treason-trial-200616234247673.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Killing of Rayshard Brooks]]
**Former [[Atlanta Police Department|Atlanta Police]] officer Garrett Rolfe is charged with [[murder (United States law)|murder]] and 10 other crimes in the death of Rayshard Brooks. Brooks was shot twice in the back after he fled from an attempted [[driving under the influence|DUI]] arrest and stole another officer's taser. This officer, Devin Brosnan, has been charged with [[aggravated assault]] and two other crimes in the case. [https://www.npr.org/sections/live-updates-protests-for-racial-justice/2020/06/17/879509659/former-atlanta-police-officer-who-shot-rayshard-brooks-charged-with-felony-murde (NPR)] 

;Politics and elections
*The [[Supreme Council (Kyrgyzstan)|Supreme Council]] of [[Kyrgyzstan]] confirms former first deputy prime minister [[Kubatbek Boronov]] as the new [[Prime Minister of Kyrgyzstan|prime minister]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-kyrgyzstan-pm/kyrgyzstans-parliament-confirms-boronov-as-prime-minister-idUSKBN23O0VY?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Vanuatu]]'s opposition leader [[Ralph Regenvanu]] says he is taking the decision to suspend his party from [[parliament of Vanuatu|parliament]] to the Supreme Court, saying the decision was an "outrage". [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/419236/vanuatu-opposition-taking-suspension-to-court (RNZ)]
*[[Cook Islands]] [[Prime Minister of the Cook Islands|Prime Minister]] [[Henry Puna]] says he is stepping down in September after nearly a decade in power. His deputy and Finance Minister [[Mark Brown (Cook Islands)|Mark Brown]] will take over. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/419204/the-cook-islands-pm-to-stand-down-in-september (RNZ)]

;Science and technology
*The [[Department of Telecommunications|Indian Department of Telecommunications]] bars the [[government of India|state]]-run telecommunication company [[Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited]] from upgrading its [[4G]] network with Chinese equipment, as tensions between [[India]] and China mount over the [[2020 China–India skirmishes|recent border skirmishes]]. [https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/government-to-ask-state-run-operator-bsnl-to-not-use-chinese-equipment-to-upgrade-4g-facilities-after-ladakh-clash-sources-2247969 (NDTV)]
